text:
Tim Stützle has 23 points in 18 games and is playing 21.9 minutes a night, and Ottawa's own team channel is calling it a "Different Level This Year." The numbers mostly agree. With him on the ice at 5v5 the Senators get 56.8% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances), 6.3 points better than when he sits.

Some of it will cool. He has 9 goals on 5.8 expected and is shooting 21%, against 18% last season, and that finishing rate rarely holds. His last ten games already look more normal: four goals on 3.5 expected.

What should last is the playmaking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards, and he carried the puck in on 62% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey's catch was defense: opponents got more chances with him on the ice than with almost any forward. That is the part TSN's Mike Johnson was talking about with his 200-foot game, and the part we'd watch.
headline: Stützle is driving Ottawa, and finishing hot
